speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are presenting with increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of painful urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, can you tell me exactly when your knee symptoms started and if the pain feels better or worse at night?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's Syndrome)

Thank you for those details; the combination of recent joint inflammation (ankle, now knee), urethritis (painful urination), and your history of sexual activity with multiple partners strongly suggests reactive arthritis. Given your anxiety, I want to confirm if you have any eye pain, redness, or changes in vision, and whether you have noticed a rash on your palms or soles?
